cards.method: Instrumental variables / 2SLS (a three-part formula) + weak-instruments / Wu-Hausman / Sargan diagnostics
cards.when: endogenous regressor(s) — the regressor is correlated with the error (simultaneity/omitted variables/measurement error); you have valid external instruments; you want a consistent causal estimate with 2SLS + full identification/endogeneity/over-identification diagnostics
cards.when_not: all regressors are exogenous (use OLS); fewer instruments than endogenous regressors (under-identified); weak instruments (the weak-IV bias calls for Anderson-Rubin or weak-IV-robust inference); panel fixed-effects IV -> #33; ML-driven high-dimensional controls -> #45

alternatives.criterion: the classic two-part IV formula 'y ~ x | z'
high-dimensional fixed effects + IV in the same fit (panel)
many/non-linear controls, ML nuisance, debiased inference
outliers or heavy tails -> a robust IV fit

output_key_fields: coefficients / coef_table: the 2SLS estimates + Estimate/Std. Error/t/p (the structural equation)
conf_int: coefficient CIs at conf_level; sigma/df_residual/nobs/r_squared/adj_r_squared
n_endogenous / n_instruments: the identification counts (over-identified <=> excluded instruments > endogenous regressors)
weak_instruments: a list {df1,df2,statistic,p_value} PER endogenous regressor (the first-stage F); weak_instruments_flag = any F<10 (Staiger-Stock)
wu_hausman: {df1,df2,statistic,p_value}, the endogeneity test (rejection -> the regressor really is endogenous, IV is justified)
sargan: {df1, df2, statistic, p_value}, the over-identification test; df1=0 with a blank statistic when just-identified; plus the overidentified flag
diagnostics: the full table (chart-data); fitted/residuals: chart-data
interpretation_traps: three-part only: 'y ~ exog | endog | instruments'; a 2-part formula is blocked (go to #34 AER); an explicit gate on the number of RHS parts
weak instruments: F<10 (weak_instruments_flag) => 2SLS bias + invalid standard CIs -> use weak-IV-robust inference; do NOT trust coef_table
the Sargan test is meaningful ONLY when the model is over-identified (df1>0); just-identified gives df1=0 and a blank value — not an error, there is simply no test
Wu-Hausman: if it is NOT rejected, OLS is consistent+efficient — IV only loses efficiency (larger SE)
method='M'/'MM' changes the estimator (robust), not only the SE; the diagnostics are interpreted on the robust fit
sources: Fox, Kleiber & Zeileis (instrumental-variables regression by two-stage least squares)
Wu 1973 / Hausman 1978 endogeneity test; Staiger & Stock 1997 (Econometrica 65:557) the weak-instruments F>10 rule

cards.method: Heterogeneity-robust dynamic DiD event study (de Chaisemartin & D'Haultfoeuille; non-binary/non-absorbing treatments)
cards.when: a staggered panel where the treatment is non-binary AND/OR non-absorbing (it can switch off or change intensity) and past treatments affect the current outcome; you want dynamic event-study effects + a placebo pre-trends test + an average total effect, robust to heterogeneous effects (without the negative-weights bias of the TWFE)
cards.when_not: the treatment is binary AND absorbing (clean staggered adoption) -> #36/#37, which are more direct; a simple 2x2 -> an interaction in #33; heterogeneity by covariates (CATE) rather than by event time -> #44

alternatives.criterion: the treatment is binary & absorbing; a doubly-robust ATT(g,t) + bootstrap bands
an absorbing design; imputation-based, analytic SE, speed
heterogeneity by covariates (CATE) rather than by relative event time
robustness to parallel-trends violations; it REQUIRES reordering coef_b/coef_vcov into chronological order (pre-periods=placebos first) before chaining

output_key_fields: estimate/se/lb_ci/ub_ci in effects: the event-study path — the dynamic treatment effects per relative period
ate_estimate/ate_available: the average total effect per unit of treatment (blank and False when trends_lin=True)
estimate/se in placebos: the placebo (pre-trend) estimators — E[placebo]=0 under parallel trends and no anticipation
p_jointeffects (effects>=2) / p_jointplacebo (placebo>=2): the joint tests; p_equality_effects when effects_equal=True
coef_b / coef_vcov: the full coefficient vector + its covariance, ordered [effects.., placebos..] with the post-periods first; for #168 reorder them chronologically, the placebos first
interpretation_traps: chaining TRAP for #168: coef_b is ordered [effects.., placebos..], post-periods first, while #168 expects CHRONOLOGICAL order (pre-periods first, with numPrePeriods equal to the number of placebos); passing coef_b AS IS produces silently wrong robust intervals — reorder it first
a placebo ~0 SUPPORTS (does not prove) parallel trends/no anticipation; a high p_jointplacebo means the hypothesis is not rejected
trends_lin=True => the ATE is NOT computed (ate_available=False, ate_estimate blank) — do not read it as 0
placebo>effects: the routine SILENTLY clamps placebo down to effects -> the wrapper hard-blocks it, so there is no silent result
a gap in a core column makes the routine silently drop rows (a partial sample) -> the wrapper hard-blocks it; the full sample is required
ci_level>=100 is accepted silently by the routine -> the wrapper blocks it; it must lie in (0,100)
a bootstrap gives stochastic standard errors; the seed (default 2025) makes them reproducible; the analytical standard errors are deterministic
sources: de Chaisemartin & D'Haultfoeuille 2020 AER 110(9) (fuzzy DiD / heterogeneous treatment effects)
de Chaisemartin & D'Haultfoeuille 2024 Econometrics Journal (dynamic/event-study non-absorbing DiD)
Rambachan & Roth 2023 ReStud (a more credible approach to parallel trends) — the consumer of coef_b/coef_vcov

cards.method: Goodman-Bacon decomposition of the TWFE DiD coefficient (staggered adoption)
cards.when: you ran a two-way fixed-effects DiD (unit+time FE) on a panel with STAGGERED adoption of the intervention and you want to see WHAT the single TWFE coefficient is made of — which 2x2 comparisons feed it and with what weights
cards.when_not: an unbalanced panel (it fails deliberately); simultaneous adoption by everyone (no staggered variation, so the decomposition is trivial); you want an ESTIMATOR that is unbiased under staggering — that is #36/#37, not a diagnostic; a continuous or non-binary treatment

alternatives.criterion: you want an UNBIASED group-time ATT rather than a diagnostic; a never/late-treated control group exists
you want an efficient imputation estimator robust to heterogeneity
you want cohort-interacted event-study estimates, not a diagnosis of the TWFE

output_key_fields: two_by_twos: a data_frame per 2x2 comparison {treated, untreated (99999=never-treated), estimate, weight, type}
type_summary: aggregate weights + the weighted mean estimate per comparison type (chart-data for the Goodman-Bacon table)
twfe_estimate: the overall TWFE beta as a weighted-average identity (= sum(w*est); with covariates = Omega*beta_hat_w + (1-Omega)*sum(w*est))
total_weight: the sum of the 2x2 weights (~1); n_2x2: the number of comparisons
has_covariates/within_estimate/within_weight: the share and estimate of the within component (Omega, beta_hat_w); blank without covariates
interpretation_traps: WATCH the 'Later vs Earlier Treated' comparison: it uses ALREADY-treated units as controls -> a forbidden comparison; a LARGE weight here means the TWFE is contaminated by negative-weighting/heterogeneity bias
untreated=99999 denotes the never-treated group (the 'clean' 'Treated vs Untreated' type); it is not a real time value
negative weights, or negative estimates under staggering, signal that the TWFE coefficient may carry the wrong sign -> move to an unbiased estimator (#36/#37)
with time-varying covariates the within component enters (Omega>0); the identity still holds, but the decomposition approximates the TWFE through FWL
it REQUIRES a strongly balanced panel; an unbalanced one -> a hard error (not a silent mistake)
sources: Goodman-Bacon 2021 (J. Econometrics 225:254, 'Difference-in-Differences with Variation in Treatment Timing')
the TWFE identity was verified numerically against lm(y ~ treated + factor(id) + factor(time)) (exact)

cards.method: Honest/robust inference under relaxed parallel trends (Rambachan-Roth sensitivity analysis)
cards.when: you have an event-study/DiD estimate (betahat + vcov per period) and you want an interval that does NOT break down when the parallel-trends assumption is violated slightly; the sensitivity of the inference to that violation
cards.when_not: you have no per-period event-study coefficients (an upstream leads/lags estimation is needed); a single post-period with no pre-periods (no basis for relative magnitudes); you do not care about robustness to parallel trends (the classic CI suffices)

alternatives.criterion: when the violation is expected to be SMOOTH (bounded curvature of the trend) — you parameterise it with M
when you do not want to choose M in absolute units — you bound the post-period violation as a multiple (Mbar) of the observed pre-period violation

alternatives.alt: #33 fx_fit event study, without the honest correction
alternatives.criterion: when you are willing to assume strict parallel trends (no sensitivity analysis)

output_key_fields: results: a data_frame lb/ub per value of M (smoothness) or Mbar (relmag) — chart-data for a sensitivity plot
lb/ub: numeric vectors of the robust CI bounds per value of the bound
method: the CI method that was used (FLCI/Conditional/C-F/C-LF)
Delta: the restriction set (DeltaSD for smoothness, DeltaRM for relmag, Original for the baseline)
M (smoothness) / Mbar (relmag): the value of the bound in each row; numPrePeriods/numPostPeriods/alpha
interpretation_traps: the CI WIDENS as M/Mbar grows — that is the point (robustness), not a problem
the breakdown value = the largest M/Mbar at which the CI does NOT contain 0; compare it with honest_original_cs (the baseline)
Mbar=1 (relmag) => the post-period violation is allowed to be as large as the LARGEST pre-period violation — often the natural reference
M is in ABSOLUTE units (the maximum second difference); Mbar is RELATIVE (in units of the pre-trend) — do not confuse them
betahat/sigma MUST be in time order (pre then post, or consistent with the indices); the wrong order -> a silently wrong CI
negative M or Mbar are accepted silently by the routine — they are blocked here (gate)
sources: Rambachan & Roth 2023, 'A More Credible Approach to Parallel Trends', Review of Economic Studies 90(5):2555-2591

cards.method: RD with multiple cutoffs / multiple scores (multi-cutoff & multi-score RD, robust bias-corrected)
cards.when: an RD design with MULTIPLE cutoffs (rdmc: C varies by unit) or cumulative cutoffs on one score (rdms); you want a pooled estimand + per-cutoff estimates, robust bias-corrected (Cattaneo-Titiunik-Vazquez-Bare)
cards.when_not: a single cutoff -> #38; a manipulation or density test (McCrary); sharp versus fuzzy without multiple cutoffs; a two-score design with a second running variable (deliberately excluded — the range matrix is fragile)

alternatives.criterion: a single cutoff (single-cutoff sharp/fuzzy RD)
parametric/non-parametric RD with an IK bandwidth, one cutoff
cumulative cutoffs on ONE score & you want a pooled estimand
conventional (not robust bias-corrected) p-values/CI for comparison

output_key_fields: pooled: {tau, se, pv, ci_l, ci_r, hl, hr, Nhl, Nhr} — the pooled estimand (always for rd_multi_cutoff; for rd_multi_score only with xnorm, otherwise available=False)
per_cutoff: a data_frame {cutoff, coef, se, ci_l, ci_r, pv, Nh_left, Nh_right, Nh_total[, weight]} = chart-data per cutoff
weighted (rdmc): {coef, se, pv, ci_l, ci_r} — the weighted average of all cutoff-specific estimates
cutoffs / n_cutoffs: the cutoff values (rdmc: sort(unique(C)); rdms: C as supplied)
cfail / n_failed: the cutoffs where the RD fit failed (degeneracy); n_failed>0 -> a suspect estimate
kernel / p / bwselect / level / conventional: the settings that were actually used
interpretation_traps: rdmc: C is a per-observation cutoff variable (the SAME length as X); rdms: C is a vector of cutoff values — do not confuse them (a wrong length -> silent recycling, blocked by a gate)
a gap in Y, X or the fuzzy assignment is ignored SILENTLY (N falls with no warning) -> a gate forbids gaps
the rd_multi_score pooled estimate is blank without xnorm; check the pooled 'available' flag before reading its tau
robust bias-corrected (the default): the CI is NOT symmetric around the (conventional) coefficient — do not read it as coef±1.96·se
cutoff-specific estimates at cutoffs with few observations (a small Nh_total) are noisy; look at Nh_total/n_failed
a single cutoff in rd_multi_cutoff gives a cryptic error; use #38 (a gate here requires at least two cutoffs)
sources: Cattaneo, Titiunik & Vazquez-Bare (2020), 'Analysis of RD Designs with Multiple Cutoffs or Multiple Scores', Stata Journal 20(4):866-891
Calonico, Cattaneo & Titiunik 2014 Econometrica 82:2295 (robust bias-corrected inference — the backbone of this card)
Cattaneo, Idrobo & Titiunik (2024) 'A Practical Introduction to RD Designs: Extensions' (CUP Elements) §multi-cutoff/multi-score

cards.method: Sensitivity analysis to unobserved confounding / omitted-variable bias (robustness value + OVB bounds)
cards.when: you have estimated a treatment effect with OLS (selection on observables) and you want to quantify how strong an UNOBSERVED confounder would have to be to change/eliminate the result (the robustness value, partial R², OVB-adjusted bounds relative to benchmark covariates)
cards.when_not: there is no credible linear design (RD/DiD/IV/synthetic control -> #38-#45); you want a point-identified effect under confounding (that needs a design, not a sensitivity analysis); a non-linear or GLM outcome (the least-squares route does not apply); pre-trend sensitivity in an event study (-> #168)

alternatives.criterion: you want heterogeneous effects under unconfoundedness, not a diagnosis of its violation
high-dimensional controls / debiased estimation instead of post-hoc sensitivity analysis
a valid instrument exists -> point identification instead of bounds
you want hypothetical confounding scenarios without a benchmark covariate (scoped out here)

output_key_fields: robustness_value (rv_q): how much partial R² (of a confounder with BOTH the treatment AND the outcome) is needed to reduce the effect by q·100%; close to 0 = fragile
robustness_value_alpha (rv_qa): the same, but for statistical non-significance at alpha
partial_r2_treatment (r2yd_x): the partial R² of the treatment with the outcome; an upper bound on what the treatment explains given the controls
ovb_bounds: a table per (benchmark × kd/ky) with adjusted_estimate/se/lower_CI/upper_CI — the effect IF the confounder were kd/ky times stronger than the benchmark covariate
unadjusted_estimate/se/t_statistic/dof: the original OLS estimate + the degrees of freedom
interpretation_traps: the RV is NOT a p-value: a small RV = little confounder strength is required = a fragile result (not the other way round)
reduce=True (the default) assumes the confounder REDUCES the effect; if the confounding would inflate it instead, set reduce=False
the bounds are conditional on the assumption 'kd times stronger than the benchmark' — their credibility rests on whether the benchmark covariate really is comparable to the plausible confounder
sensitivity ≠ identification: the tool does NOT correct the bias; it only says how much confounding would overturn it (design-based safety remains the user's responsibility)
least squares only: the alternative fixed-effects, formula and numeric routes are deliberately excluded; supply a fitted least-squares model, or a formula with its data
sources: Cinelli & Hazlett (2020), 'Making Sense of Sensitivity: Extending Omitted Variable Bias', JRSS-B 82(1):39-67
Cinelli, Ferwerda & Hazlett 2020 (sensitivity analysis tools for OLS, SSRN 3588978)
precondition_tools: sens_analyze (the formula+data route: it fits the lm internally)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_csv_data (load the cross-section before the formula+data route)
c00_data_utilities/analytic_ols_closed.ols_regress (an ALREADY fitted least-squares model is passed as the object; the consuming route accepts nothing else)

cards.method: IPW / double-ML treatment effects (ATE/ATET, IV-LATE/LATT, causal mediation)
cards.when: selection-on-observables treatment evaluation with ready-made y/d/x vectors (NOT a formula): DML-ATE for a discrete treatment (cw_treatment_dml); IPW ATE/ATET for a binary treatment (cw_treatment_ipw); IV-LATE/LATT with a binary instrument (cw_late_ipw); a direct/indirect split through a mediator (cw_mediation_dml)
cards.when_not: you have no observable confounders (unconfoundedness fails -> RD/DiD/synthetic control); a panel with staggered adoption (-> #36/#37/#43); heterogeneous CATE by covariate (-> #44); linear IV with a formula (-> #34/#33); a time-series intervention (-> #90)

alternatives.criterion: you want the full double-ML framework (random-forest or elastic-net learners, ATTE, tuning) rather than IPW or the efficient score
heterogeneous CATE by covariate, not only a population ATE
linear 2SLS IV with a formula (a continuous treatment/instrument; a global LATE assuming linearity)
you want doubly-robust/ML nuisance (Neyman orthogonality) rather than plain IPW; or a multi-valued discrete treatment

output_key_fields: effect: the main causal effect (ATE/ATET/LATE/LATT); se: the standard error; pval: the p-value
cw_treatment_ipw: y1/y0 (the mean potential outcomes); estimand 'ATE'/'ATET'
cw_late_ipw: first (+se_first/pval_first) = the complier share/first stage; ITT (+se_ITT/pval_ITT) = intention to treat
cw_mediation_dml: ate + dir_treat/dir_control (natural direct) + indir_treat/indir_control (natural indirect); se/pval of length 6 (a 3x6 results matrix)
ntrimmed: the number of observations dropped because of extreme propensity scores (an overlap diagnostic)
interpretation_traps: unconfoundedness is an UNTESTABLE assumption — the SE do not certify it; a high ntrimmed = weak overlap, and the estimate then rests on a few units
the IV-LATE (cw_late_ipw) is an effect ONLY on the compliers, not on the population; a small 'first' -> a weak instrument, the effect explodes/is unstable
mediation (cw_mediation_dml) ADDITIONALLY requires sequential ignorability of the mediator; the direct+indirect split is not fully experimentally identified
stochasticity: treatDML/medDML (cross-fitting fold splits) & treatweight/lateweight (bootstrap) -> the same effect ONLY with the same seed (default 2025)
MLmethod='lasso' in cw_mediation_dml (hdm rlasso) can throw 'subscript out of bounds' at small n -> use 'parametric'/'randomforest' or a larger sample
d must be 0/1 (treatweight/lateweight/medDML) & z 0/1 (lateweight); a non-binary d/z is blocked (otherwise a cryptic 'y values must be 0<=y<=1' from the probit)
sources: Chernozhukov et al. 2018, 'Double/debiased machine learning', Econometrics Journal 21:C1-C68
Farbmacher, Huber, Laffers, Langen, Spindler 2022, 'Causal mediation analysis with double machine learning', Econometrics Journal 25:277-300
Tchetgen Tchetgen & Shpitser 2012 (Annals of Statistics 40:1816) — semiparametric mediation
precondition_tools: cw_treatment_ipw (unconfoundedness + common support: check ntrimmed/overlap before the ATE)
cw_late_ipw (the first stage 'first' = the complier share: a weak instrument if it is ~0)
c07_causality_policy/double_debiased.dml_irm (cross-check the ATE with an independent DML implementation)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the tabular dataset; build the y/d/x/z/m vectors)

cards.method: Generalized Method of Moments (linear IV / moment conditions) + the Hansen-Sargan J test
cards.when: over-identified linear IV / moment-condition estimation (Euler equations, macro/finance) where you want efficient GMM + HAC-robust inference + a test of instrument validity (Hansen J)
cards.when_not: just-identified 2SLS with a single endogenous regressor (-> #34/#165); non-linear user-supplied moment functions (NOT exposed — that would be an evaluation surface); dynamic panel GMM (Arellano-Bond -> #47)

alternatives.criterion: just-identified 2SLS, or you want rich IV diagnostics (the weak-instruments F, Wu-Hausman endogeneity, Sargan)
classic 2SLS with the simple formula 'y ~ x | z'
high-dimensional fixed effects + IV together
you want a 2SLS-equivalent estimate (identity weighting) rather than efficient GMM

output_key_fields: coefficients: a named numeric vector — the coefficient estimates (e.g. the slope on the endogenous regressor)
coef_table: a matrix Estimate/Std. Error/z value/Pr(>|z|) — asymptotic normal inference (the SE come from the chosen vcov)
vcov / std_errors: the covariance matrix of the coefficients and the SE (they correspond to the vcov argument)
J_test: {statistic, df, p_value}, the Hansen over-identification test; df = instruments - coefficients (df=0 means just-identified, and the p-value is blank)
df / nobs / type / wmatrix / vcov_type: the over-identifying degrees of freedom, the observations left after the gap gate, and the estimator settings
interpretation_traps: Hansen J: a SMALL p_value (rejecting H0) => the instruments/moment conditions are NOT valid (misspecification), NOT 'a significant result'
just-identified (df=0): the J test is NOT defined — gmm_j_test returns a statistic near 0 with a note and a blank p-value; do not read it as a 'perfect fit'
the estimator drops rows with gaps SILENTLY (only a warning) — the wrapper blocks that with a gate; nobs counts the rows after cleaning
vcov='HAC' (the default): autocorrelation-robust — for a pure cross-section prefer vcov='iid'/'MDS'; the SE change substantially with the vcov
under-identification (moments < coefficients) is blocked by a clean gate before the call — add instruments
SECURITY: only the formula/linear interface is exposed; a user-supplied moment function (gmm(g=<fn>)) is NOT supported (an eval surface)
sources: Hansen (1982) 'Large Sample Properties of GMM Estimators', Econometrica 50:1029
Chaussé 2010 JSS 34(11) (computing generalized method of moments estimators)
Hall (2005) Generalized Method of Moments, Oxford — the Sargan-Hansen J over-identification test
precondition_tools: gmm_j_test (the Hansen-Sargan J test after estimation: rejecting H0 -> the instruments/moment conditions are NOT valid)
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_suite.unitroot_adf (stationarity of the series before GMM on time series — a HAC vcov presupposes weak dependence)

cards.when: one or a few treated units and a donor pool, where neither synthetic control nor difference-in-differences alone is convincing
cards.when_not: there is no pre-treatment period long enough to fit unit weights; the donor pool contains units affected by the treatment

alternatives.criterion: one treated unit, exact pre-treatment match wanted
parallel trends is credible without weighting
you want unit and time weights plus a DiD structure

output_key_fields: att: the estimated effect
unit_weights, time_weights: the two weightings that define the estimator
se: jackknife or placebo standard error
pre_treatment_fit: how well the weighted control tracked before treatment
interpretation_traps: synthetic DiD is a WEIGHTED DiD, so it relaxes parallel trends but does not remove the assumption -- it only makes it more plausible
inference with one treated unit rests on placebo distributions, not asymptotics; the p-value is bounded below by one over the donor count
a poor pre-treatment fit invalidates the whole design and cannot be fixed by more donors
sources: Arkhangelsky, Athey, Hirshberg, Imbens & Wager 2021 (American Economic Review 111:4088-4118)

cards.method: Heterogeneity-robust staggered DiD: Sun-Abraham, ETWFE, stacked, did2s and LP-DiD
cards.when: treatment starts at different times for different units, where two-way fixed effects can produce an estimate of the wrong sign entirely
cards.when_not: treatment starts at one date for everyone, where ordinary DiD is fine; there are no never-treated or not-yet-treated units to serve as controls

alternatives.criterion: you want an event study free of contamination
you want a regression-based estimator with the same robustness
you want a transparent design or a two-stage estimator

output_key_fields: att: the overall effect and the effect by cohort and by relative period
event_study: dynamic effects around the treatment date
negative_weights: whether the naive TWFE estimator carries them
cohorts: the treatment timing groups
interpretation_traps: TWO-WAY FIXED EFFECTS WITH STAGGERED TIMING USES ALREADY-TREATED UNITS AS CONTROLS, which can produce negative weights and an estimate opposite in sign to every underlying effect
an event-study plot from a naive interacted regression is contaminated across relative periods; the interaction-weighted estimator exists to fix exactly that
the comparison group -- never treated versus not yet treated -- changes the estimand, and both should be reported

cards.when: checking whether units sorted around the cut-off, which would invalidate the entire discontinuity design
cards.when_not: the running variable is coarsely discretised so a density test is not meaningful; assignment is verifiably outside the units' control

alternatives.criterion: the classic binned test
a local polynomial density test with no pre-binning
a complementary check

output_key_fields: statistic, p_value: the manipulation test
density_left, density_right: estimated densities either side
discontinuity: the estimated jump in the density
bandwidth: the bandwidth used
interpretation_traps: A DENSITY DISCONTINUITY INVALIDATES THE DESIGN; this test is not a robustness check to be relegated to an appendix
the test has low power in small samples, so passing it is weak evidence of no manipulation
heaping at round numbers produces a spurious rejection that has nothing to do with strategic sorting

cards.when: treating a narrow window around the cut-off as a randomised experiment, which needs no continuity assumption and no extrapolation
cards.when_not: no window is narrow enough for randomisation to be credible; the running variable is continuous and the design has plenty of data for a local polynomial

alternatives.criterion: the standard approach
the running variable is discrete or the sample is small
manipulation itself is the object of study

output_key_fields: effect: the randomisation-based estimate
window: the selected window and how it was chosen
balance: covariate balance inside the window
p_value: randomisation-inference p-value
interpretation_traps: the WINDOW SELECTION is the identifying assumption; selecting it to maximise the effect is specification search
inside the window the design is a small experiment, so power is usually very low and a null is uninformative
covariate balance inside the window is the only evidence for the assumption and must be reported
sources: Cattaneo, Frandsen & Titiunik 2015 (Journal of Causal Inference 3:1-24)
Cattaneo, Idrobo & Titiunik 2024, A Practical Introduction to Regression Discontinuity Designs: Extensions

cards.when: showing a conditional relationship without imposing a functional form, with bands that are actually valid rather than decorative
cards.when_not: you need the parameter of a specific functional form; the sample is too small for binning to leave anything in each bin

alternatives.criterion: exploratory only
you want a defensible plot with valid bands
you want the curve rather than the bins

output_key_fields: bins: bin means of the outcome and the running variable
n_bins: the number chosen and the rule that chose it
conf_band: valid uniform bands
shape_tests: tests of linearity, monotonicity or a specified polynomial
interpretation_traps: THE NUMBER OF BINS IS NOT A COSMETIC CHOICE -- the conventional twenty is arbitrary and can hide or manufacture nonlinearity; use the data-driven rule
naive binscatter bands are far too narrow because they ignore the binning; the modern implementation corrects this
residualising on covariates before binning changes the interpretation from a conditional mean to a partial one, and the two are often confused
sources: Cattaneo, Crump, Farrell & Feng 2024 (Review of Economics and Statistics, forthcoming)

cards.method: Wild cluster bootstrap and randomisation inference for policy designs
cards.when: treatment is assigned at a group level and the number of groups is small, where cluster-robust standard errors over-reject severely
cards.when_not: there are many clusters and ordinary cluster-robust inference is adequate

alternatives.criterion: many clusters
few clusters
the assignment mechanism is known

output_key_fields: p_value: bootstrap or randomisation p-value
conf_int: interval by test inversion
n_clusters: the count that determines reliability
over_rejection_diagnostic: comparison with the naive cluster-robust p-value
interpretation_traps: WITH FEWER THAN ROUGHLY FIVE CLUSTERS no method restores correct size; report the cluster count, not just a p-value
Rademacher weights impose a floor on the attainable p-value that depends on the cluster count
clustering at the wrong level -- finer than assignment -- understates standard errors regardless of the method
sources: Cameron, Gelbach & Miller 2008 (Review of Economics and Statistics 90:414-427)

cards.method: Weak-instrument-robust inference: Anderson-Rubin, CLR, LIML and JIVE
cards.when: the instruments are weak, where two-stage least squares is biased toward the ordinary least squares estimate and its confidence interval has no coverage
cards.when_not: the first stage is strong by any measure and conventional inference is fine

alternatives.criterion: fully robust to weak instruments, exact coverage
robust and more powerful than Anderson-Rubin
less biased point estimates under many weak instruments

output_key_fields: ar_statistic, clr_statistic: weak-instrument-robust tests
conf_set: which may be unbounded or empty -- both are meaningful
first_stage_f: the effective F statistic
liml, jive: alternative point estimates
interpretation_traps: AN UNBOUNDED CONFIDENCE SET IS THE CORRECT ANSWER when instruments are weak -- it is information, not a failure, and reporting a tight 2SLS interval instead is the error
an EMPTY confidence set means the model is rejected at that level, which is also informative
the rule-of-thumb first-stage F of 10 is not valid with multiple endogenous regressors or non-homoskedastic errors; use the effective F
sources: Andrews, Stock & Sun 2019 (Annual Review of Economics 11:727)

cards.when: the treatment may shift the whole distribution rather than just its mean, and the mean can hide offsetting effects at different quantiles
cards.when_not: you only need the mean effect; the sample is too small for quantile estimates at the tails

alternatives.criterion: the mean is the object of interest
a nonlinear DiD that respects the distribution
you want the effect at specified quantiles

output_key_fields: qte: the effect at each requested quantile
conf_band: bands, which must be uniform if the whole curve is interpreted
distributional_test: test of a constant effect across quantiles
counterfactual_distribution: the untreated distribution for the treated
interpretation_traps: a QUANTILE TREATMENT EFFECT IS NOT THE EFFECT ON A GIVEN UNIT unless ranks are preserved; it compares distributions, not individuals
changes-in-changes replaces parallel trends with a monotonicity assumption -- weaker in some respects, stronger in others, not simply better
pointwise quantile bands read as a curve overstate precision; a uniform band is needed for statements about the shape

cards.method: Meta-learners for conditional average treatment effects: S, T, X, residual and doubly-robust
cards.when: the effect varies across units and you want to estimate that variation with machine learning rather than pre-specified interactions
cards.when_not: the sample is too small for the effect surface to be estimated; you only need the average effect

alternatives.criterion: one model with treatment as a feature; simplest, biased toward zero heterogeneity
separate models per arm; unbiased but noisy with imbalanced arms
doubly robust, the usual default

output_key_fields: cate: the estimated effect per unit
ate: the average, which should agree with a direct estimate
heterogeneity_test: whether the effect genuinely varies
feature_importance: which covariates drive the variation
interpretation_traps: THE S-LEARNER SHRINKS HETEROGENEITY TOWARD ZERO because a single model can ignore the treatment feature; a flat CATE from it is not evidence of homogeneity
individual CATE estimates are very noisy; they support group-level statements, not unit-level decisions, without further calibration
cross-fitting is required for valid inference, and without it the confidence intervals are meaningless
sources: Kunzel, Sekhon, Bickel & Yu 2019 (Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 116:4156-4165)

cards.method: Policy learning and optimal assignment rules
cards.when: turning heterogeneous effect estimates into a decision rule about who should be treated, subject to a budget or a simplicity constraint
cards.when_not: the effect is homogeneous, where the rule is trivial; the CATE estimates are too noisy to support any rule

alternatives.criterion: no constraint, simplest rule
you need an interpretable rule
only a share can be treated

output_key_fields: policy: the learned assignment rule
value: estimated policy value against the baseline
regret: distance from the infeasible optimal rule
treated_share: the share the rule assigns
interpretation_traps: POLICY VALUE ESTIMATED ON THE SAME DATA THAT LEARNED THE POLICY IS OPTIMISTIC; honest evaluation needs a held-out sample or cross-fitting
a rule built from noisy CATE estimates can be worse than treating everyone or no one; always compare against both baselines
constraining a rule to be interpretable costs policy value, and that cost should be quantified rather than ignored

cards.method: Panel event-study construction and pre-trend testing
cards.when: building the relative-time indicators an event study needs and testing the pre-trends the design depends on
cards.when_not: there is no panel dimension; treatment timing is not observed at unit level

alternatives.alt: event-study plot with leads and lags
alternatives.criterion: the standard presentation
a formal test rather than a visual one
you want to relax parallel trends rather than test it

output_key_fields: coefficients: effect per relative period, with the omitted base period stated
pretrend_test: joint test that pre-treatment coefficients are zero
event_window: the relative periods estimated
binned_endpoints: whether distant periods were binned
interpretation_traps: A PRE-TREND TEST THAT FAILS TO REJECT IS WEAK EVIDENCE -- these tests have low power, and pre-testing itself distorts the subsequent inference
the omitted base period is a normalisation; changing it shifts every coefficient and can flip the visual impression entirely
distant relative periods are estimated on few units and must usually be binned, which is a choice that affects the picture

cards.method: Marginal effects, contrasts and predictions for any fitted model
cards.when: turning coefficients from a nonlinear model into quantities that can be read -- effects on the outcome scale, at stated covariate values
cards.when_not: the model is linear with no interactions, where the coefficient already is the marginal effect

alternatives.criterion: the average derivative across the sample
the derivative at one representative point
comparisons between stated covariate profiles

output_key_fields: marginal_effects: the requested effects with delta-method standard errors
contrasts: differences between specified profiles
predictions: fitted values at stated covariate values
at: the covariate values the effects were evaluated at
interpretation_traps: AVERAGE MARGINAL EFFECTS AND EFFECTS AT THE MEAN ARE DIFFERENT QUANTITIES and can differ substantially in a nonlinear model; which was computed must be stated
the delta method assumes the transformation is approximately linear over the sampling distribution, which fails for ratios and near boundaries
an 'effect at the mean' can be evaluated at a covariate combination that exists in no observation, particularly with dummies

cards.when: the design has several high-dimensional fixed effects -- firm, worker, year -- that cannot be estimated as dummies
cards.when_not: there is one low-dimensional fixed effect, where dummies are simpler and give the coefficients directly

alternatives.criterion: few levels
one fixed effect
several high-dimensional effects

output_key_fields: params: coefficients on the non-absorbed regressors
absorbed: the fixed effects removed and their level counts
converged: whether the projection algorithm converged
connected_components: identification structure across the effect dimensions
interpretation_traps: with two or more high-dimensional effects the parameters are identified only WITHIN CONNECTED COMPONENTS of the bipartite mobility graph; a disconnected sample identifies less than it appears to
absorbed fixed effects are not estimated, so they cannot be reported or interpreted -- if you need them, do not absorb them
the alternating-projection algorithm converges slowly with weakly connected data, and a loose tolerance leaves bias in the coefficients
sources: Correia 2017, Linear models with high-dimensional fixed effects (unpublished manuscript)

cards.when: assembling several fitted models into one comparable table, with consistent formatting and stated standard-error types
cards.when_not: there is one model and a table adds nothing

alternatives.criterion: one model only
several specifications side by side
you want a figure rather than a table

output_key_fields: table: the assembled table
notes: standard-error type, fixed effects and sample per column
statistics: observation counts, R2 and other reported statistics
format: the output format requested
interpretation_traps: A TABLE WITHOUT ITS STANDARD-ERROR TYPE IS UNREADABLE; robust, clustered and classical errors differ by large factors and the note is not decoration
columns estimated on different samples are not comparable, and the observation count per column is what reveals that
significance stars encode arbitrary thresholds and hide the magnitude; report the estimate and its interval
